name: Ingenuity (Mars Helicopter)

site.name: Jezero Crater (Valinor Hills / Airfield Chi)
site.description: Deployed in Jezero Crater and flown across 72 sorties before coming to rest at Airfield Chi in the Valinor Hills region near Neretva Vallis.

endCause: Carbon-composite rotor blade tip damage during Flight 72 landing on January 18, 2024 permanently grounded the helicopter; final radio telemetry via Perseverance arrived on April 16, 2024.
scientificValue: Built as a five-flight technology demonstration for a 30-sol test window, Ingenuity operated for nearly three Earth years and completed 72 flights totaling 17.0 kilometers. It proved sustained aerodynamic flight in Mars' thin carbon-dioxide atmosphere and pioneered aerial scouting ahead of surface rovers.
kidSummary: Carried beneath the Perseverance rover, this lightweight twin-rotor helicopter achieved the first powered flight on another planet—completing 72 flights across 17.0 kilometers in Mars' thin air.

legacy.finding: Achieved the first powered, controlled aerodynamic flight on another planet on April 19, 2021 at Wright Brothers Field in Jezero Crater.
Completed 72 flights accumulating approximately 128.8 flight minutes and 17.0 kilometers of horizontal ground distance.
Delivered a final April 16, 2024 patch transitioning onboard avionics into a long-term stationary surface weather and imagery testbed.
legacy.sourceTitle: NASA Science — Ingenuity Final Transmission Update

verificationNote: Atlas coordinates reflect the verified Mars 2020 Jezero Crater landing locus (18.4447° N, 77.4508° E); exact sub-degree coordinates of Ingenuity's final resting position at Airfield Chi (Valinor Hills) await PDS tabular confirmation.
